name: Unencrypted HTTP Endpoint
description: Unencrypted HTTP Endpoint — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Replace http:// with https:// for all external endpoints. ePHI in transit must be encrypted.

name: TLS Verification Disabled
description: TLS Verification Disabled — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Never disable TLS certificate verification. Disabling it exposes ePHI to man-in-the-middle attacks.

name: Weak Randomness in Security Context
description: Weak Randomness in Security Context — §164.312(d) — Person Authentication.
recommendation: Use secrets.token_hex() or secrets.token_urlsafe() for session tokens and authentication values.

name: Potential SQL Injection
description: Potential SQL Injection — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: Use parameterized queries. SQL injection on a patient database constitutes unauthorized ePHI access.

name: Potential PHI in Logs
description: Potential PHI in Logs — §164.312(b) — Audit Controls.
recommendation: Do not log raw patient data. Log event types and record IDs only; mask or omit PHI fields entirely.

name: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle)
description: Insecure Deserialization (Pickle) — §164.312(c)(1) — Integrity.
recommendation: pickle.loads() on untrusted data enables arbitrary code execution, risking complete ePHI compromise.

name: Hardcoded Healthcare API Credential
description: Hardcoded Healthcare API Credential — §164.308(a)(1) — Security Management Process.
recommendation: Healthcare integration credentials must be stored in environment variables or a secrets manager.

name: Hardcoded JWT / Auth Secret
description: Hardcoded JWT / Auth Secret — §164.312(d) — Person Authentication.
recommendation: JWT secrets loaded from source code allow authentication bypass. Use environment variables or a vault.

name: Debug Mode Enabled
description: Debug Mode Enabled — §164.308(a)(1) — Security Management Process.
recommendation: Disable debug mode before deployment. Stack traces and verbose errors may expose ePHI.

name: Database Connection Without Encryption Flag
description: Database Connection Without Encryption Flag — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Add SSL/TLS parameters to database URLs (e.g., ?sslmode=require) to encrypt ePHI in transit.

name: Weak Password Hashing Algorithm
description: Weak Password Hashing Algorithm — §164.312(d) — Person Authentication.
recommendation: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken for password storage. Use bcrypt, argon2, or scrypt via passlib.

name: CORS Wildcard Origin
description: CORS Wildcard Origin — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: A wildcard CORS origin allows any domain to call your API. Restrict to a known allow-list of trusted origins.

name: Insecure Session Cookie
description: Insecure Session Cookie — §164.312(e)(1) — Transmission Security.
recommendation: Session cookies must set Secure=True and HttpOnly=True to prevent ePHI session tokens from being stolen.

name: S3 Bucket Public-Read ACL
description: S3 Bucket Public-Read ACL — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: Public S3 ACLs expose all stored objects to the internet. Use private ACLs with pre-signed URLs for authorized access to ePHI.

name: Hardcoded SSN in Source
description: Hardcoded SSN in Source — §164.308(a)(1) — Security Management Process.
recommendation: Social Security Numbers must not appear in source code or test fixtures. Use synthetic or de-identified test data.

name: Unparameterized NoSQL Query
description: Unparameterized NoSQL Query — §164.312(a)(1) — Access Control.
recommendation: User-controlled input injected into NoSQL queries can bypass access controls on ePHI. Use schema validation and sanitization.

name: Plaintext ePHI Written to Disk
description: Plaintext ePHI Written to Disk — §164.312(e)(2) — Encryption.
recommendation: ePHI written to disk must be encrypted at rest. Use encrypted storage or apply AES-256 encryption before writing.

name: Cardholder PAN in Source Code
description: Cardholder PAN in Source Code — PCI-DSS Req 3.4 — Stored Cardholder Data.
recommendation: Primary Account Numbers must never appear in source code. Use tokenization or masked test surrogates.

name: CVV/CVC Storage
description: CVV/CVC Storage — PCI-DSS Req 3.3 — Prohibited Data.
recommendation: CVV/CVC codes must never be stored after authorization. Storage is prohibited regardless of encryption.

name: Magnetic Stripe Track Data
description: Magnetic Stripe Track Data — PCI-DSS Req 3.3 — Prohibited Data.
recommendation: Magnetic stripe track data must never be stored after authorization. Remove storage and retention code entirely.

name: Unencrypted Payment Endpoint
description: Unencrypted Payment Endpoint — PCI-DSS Req 4.2 — Transmission Security.
recommendation: All cardholder data transmission must use TLS 1.2+. Replace http:// with https:// on all payment endpoints.

name: Prohibited Weak Cipher
description: Prohibited Weak Cipher — PCI-DSS Req 4.2 — Transmission Security.
recommendation: DES, 3DES, and RC4 are prohibited for protecting cardholder data. Use AES-256 with GCM or CBC+HMAC.

name: Hardcoded Payment Processor Credential
description: Hardcoded Payment Processor Credential — PCI-DSS Req 6.3 — Security Vulnerabilities.
recommendation: Payment processor credentials must be stored in environment variables or a secrets manager, never in source code.

name: Card Data in Application Logs
description: Card Data in Application Logs — PCI-DSS Req 10.2 — Audit Logging.
recommendation: PAN and card data must never appear in logs. Log only masked values (last 4 digits) for audit purposes.

name: Default or Weak Credential
description: Default or Weak Credential — PCI-DSS Req 8.3 — Authentication Management.
recommendation: Default credentials fail PCI-DSS Req 8. Deploy with unique strong credentials and rotate on a defined schedule.

name: Plaintext Card Data Written to File
description: Plaintext Card Data Written to File — PCI-DSS Req 3.5 — Encryption of Stored Data.
recommendation: Stored cardholder data must be encrypted with AES-256. Never write PAN or card data to plaintext files.
compliance_ref: PCI-DSS Req 3.5 — Encryption of Stored Data

name: Missing PCI Scope Isolation
description: Missing PCI Scope Isolation — PCI-DSS Req 12.5 — Scope Management.
recommendation: Ensure cardholder data environment (CDE) systems are isolated from out-of-scope systems. Review network segmentation.

name: Personal Data in Application Logs
description: Personal Data in Application Logs — GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — Integrity and Confidentiality.
recommendation: Personal data must not appear in logs. Log event IDs only; redact or pseudonymize PII in all log outputs.

name: Third-Party Tracker Without Consent
description: Third-Party Tracker Without Consent — GDPR Art. 7 — Conditions for Consent.
recommendation: Third-party analytics and tracking require explicit prior consent under GDPR. Implement a Consent Management Platform.

name: Personal Data Written to File Unencrypted
description: Personal Data Written to File Unencrypted — GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing.
recommendation: Personal data written to files must be encrypted at rest with AES-256. Verify access controls on the file path.

name: IP Address Stored Without Masking
description: IP Address Stored Without Masking — GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) — Data Minimisation.
recommendation: IP addresses are personal data under GDPR. Anonymize the last octet before storage or document the Art. 6 legal basis.

name: Personal Data in Error Messages
description: Personal Data in Error Messages — GDPR Art. 5(1)(f) — Integrity and Confidentiality.
recommendation: Error messages must not expose personal data. Log full detail server-side only; show a generic message to end users.

name: Sensitive PII Field Without Encryption Indicator
description: Sensitive PII Field Without Encryption Indicator — GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing.
recommendation: Sensitive personal identifiers must be encrypted or pseudonymized at rest. Use column-level encryption for sensitive fields.

name: Cookie Set Without Consent Check
description: Cookie Set Without Consent Check — GDPR Art. 7 — Conditions for Consent.
recommendation: Non-essential cookies require explicit user consent before setting. Integrate a Consent Management Platform.

name: Personal Data Hashed With Weak Algorithm
description: Personal Data Hashed With Weak Algorithm — GDPR Art. 32 — Security of Processing.
recommendation: MD5/SHA-1 pseudonymization is reversible via rainbow tables. Use SHA-256 with salt, or bcrypt/argon2 for identity fields.

name: Data Transfer to Non-EEA Cloud Service
description: Data Transfer to Non-EEA Cloud Service — GDPR Art. 44 — Transfer to Third Countries.
recommendation: Transferring personal data to non-EEA processors requires SCCs or an adequacy decision. Verify data residency configuration.
compliance_ref: GDPR Art. 44 — Transfer to Third Countries

name: Missing Data Deletion / Expiry Field
description: Missing Data Deletion / Expiry Field — GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) — Storage Limitation.
recommendation: Personal data must not be retained longer than necessary. Add a deleted_at or expires_at field and enforce deletion schedules.

name: Authentication Bypass Flag
description: Authentication Bypass Flag — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: Authentication bypass flags must never be deployed. Remove entirely; use environment-gated feature flags.

name: Debug Backdoor or Maintenance Mode
description: Debug Backdoor or Maintenance Mode — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: Backdoor and maintenance-mode access paths violate SOC 2 logical access controls. Remove from production code entirely.

name: CORS Wildcard Origin
description: CORS Wildcard Origin — SOC 2 CC6.6 — External Threats.
recommendation: Wildcard CORS grants unrestricted cross-origin access. Restrict to an explicit allow-list of known trusted origins.

name: Insecure Direct Object Reference
description: Insecure Direct Object Reference — SOC 2 CC6.1 — Logical Access Controls.
recommendation: Direct use of user-supplied IDs in queries risks unauthorized data access. Verify record ownership before returning data.

name: Silent Exception Swallowing
description: Silent Exception Swallowing — SOC 2 CC7.2 — System Monitoring.
recommendation: Silent exception handling hides operational failures. Log all exceptions with context and alert on unexpected error rates.

name: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log
description: Privileged Operation Without Audit Log — SOC 2 CC7.3 — Audit Logging.
recommendation: Destructive and privileged operations must produce audit log entries. Log actor, action, timestamp, and affected resource ID.

name: Unrestricted File Upload
description: Unrestricted File Upload — SOC 2 CC6.8 — Input Validation.
recommendation: Unrestricted file uploads enable code execution and storage abuse. Validate type, size, and content before persisting.

name: HTTPS Not Enforced
description: HTTPS Not Enforced — SOC 2 CC6.7 — Transmission Controls.
recommendation: HTTPS must be enforced for all production traffic. Enable SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE before deployment.

name: Hardcoded Inter-Service Token
description: Hardcoded Inter-Service Token — SOC 2 CC6.3 — Access Provisioning.
recommendation: Inter-service credentials hardcoded in source enable lateral movement. Use a secrets manager or mTLS for service-to-service auth.

name: Test Credentials Left in Code
description: Test Credentials Left in Code — SOC 2 CC6.3 — Access Provisioning.
recommendation: Test credentials in production code violate environment separation. Remove or gate behind strict environment checks.
